In 1964 the ten-string classical guitar developed by Narciso Yepes with José Ramírez III attracted attention when he played the Concierto de Aranjuez with the Berlin Philharmonic; from 1963 he used this instrument for both recordings and performances, and the arrival of high-quality ten-string guitars drew other players in. In 2008 Mike Shishkov demonstrated a ten-string jazz guitar, and in 2009 a solid-body ten-string electric guitar with nylon strings was released.

Its first six strings can play the ordinary six-string classical guitar repertory, with added resonance; it can also be used to transcribe lute works by Bach and his contemporaries, or to play newly written ten-string guitar pieces. Other variants appear in folk music, jazz guitar demonstrations and popular music, such as the English guitar, the Brazilian folk guitar and the ten-string electric guitar.

The ten-string guitar is a chordophone, H-S 321.322-5, a general term for guitar-type instruments with ten strings, including acoustic and electric guitars in double-course and single-course variants, found mainly in classical, folk and popular music. In construction it may be a single neck with additional bass strings, or a five- or six-course arrangement; it is played with the fingers or with a plectrum. The ten-string classical guitar developed by Narciso Yepes with José Ramírez III, for example, lets six-string repertory keep its usual fingering and adds resonance; the viola caipira (country guitar) of Brazilian folk music, by contrast, is played with ten strings in five courses.
十弦吉他琴身採用歐洲雲杉或西德牌木為面板，背側板使用巴西玫瑰木或印度紫檀等硬木。: The ten-string guitar uses European spruce or west German spruce for the soundboard, and hardwoods such as Brazilian rosewood or Indian rosewood for the back and sides. The neck is of mahogany or cedar and the fretboard of ebony or rosewood. The strings are usually nylon, with wound nylon for the treble strings and copper-wound nylon or steel for the bass strings. Fittings such as the bridge and bridge pins are of ebony or an ivory substitute, and metal parts such as the frets are of nickel silver.
十弦吉他音色溫潤而富有層次感，兼具明亮與深沉的特質。其額外的弦線賦予樂器更寬廣的: The ten-string guitar has a warm, layered timbre that is both bright and deep. The extra strings give the instrument a wider range: the bass strings supply a deep, well-resonated low end, while the treble strings keep a clear, transparent quality. Its resonance is unusual in that the double courses make strings of the same pitch vibrate and resonate with one another, producing a fuller volume and a sense of space. Compared with the standard six-string guitar, the ten-string has a richer, more solid bass, close to the warm quality of the classical guitar and the harp; in the treble it combines the clarity of the electric guitar with the organic feel of a folk instrument. Its arpeggios are especially pleasing, and the timbre loses none of the guitar's approachability while gaining, through the extra strings, more layers of sound and more expressive range.
